sections.content: You know the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 21 (and *mientras* + imperfect from A2 Unit 22). Here you use it to open a memory: it describes the setting, repeated actions and feelings that lasted, and answers what life was like before one particular event changed the scene.

items.spanish: Cuando vivía en aquel vecindario, el aroma del pan entraba por el balcón cada mañana y llenaba la cocina en primavera.
items.english: When I lived in that neighbourhood, the scent of bread came in through the balcony and filled the kitchen in spring.

items.spanish: En mi infancia, los adultos se reunían mientras los niños jugaban y mi madre llamaba desde la cocina.
items.english: In my childhood, the adults gathered while the children played and my mother called from the kitchen.

items.spanish: Teníamos la costumbre de sentarnos fuera, y los mayores nos hablaban con cariño.
items.english: We used to sit outside, and the adults would speak to us affectionately.

items.spanish: Aunque vivíamos en calles distintas, todos nos conocíamos y nos saludábamos cuando pasábamos.
items.english: Although we lived on different streets, we all knew one another and said hello when we passed.

sections.content: The *imperfecto* does not say that a repeated habit ended; it lets the listener enter the background of the memory. When one event interrupts the scene, the *indefinido* tells it: *Cuando vivíamos allí, mi padre cambió de trabajo.*

sections.topic: the imperfect tense for past habits and descriptions
